required_fixes.reason: The model domain is well defined. Empty models have zero surplus. Harmlessness of deletion-only models requires the target induced-subgraph criticality assumption. Without it, contracted Heawood plus an isolated vertex at K=3 has a deletion-only quotient of surplus 1, but every quotient involving contraction has surplus at most 0. State that K is an integer, as inherited from ctx.

Correct for positive integral surplus. Qualify the overview sentence: a safe edge, or a pentagon matching that satisfies Theorem 3 safety, has negative cost. It must not assert existence of an admissible choice in every triangle-free graph; the Robertson augmentation has none of these one- or two-edge choices.

The finite-simplex argument is exact when the model set is nonempty. Explicitly assume G is nonempty; then the empty quotient supplies a proper model. For G empty there are no proper models and the displayed minima are undefined. Target applications already have G nonempty.

The neighborhood-matching argument and common-neighbor uniqueness justify the vertexwise count. The nonnegative t(2d-t-2) term and Cauchy–Schwarz prove the bound. State the radical inequality for h>=1, and handle h=0 with S=0; sqrt(h-1) is not real at h=0. The squared inequality itself also covers h=0.

Pentagon coverage follows from exclusion of safe SINGLE-edge contractions in a minimum counterexample, not from absence of pentagon two-edge reductions alone. Theta_2 plus a pendant edge has two pentagons and zero safe pentagon two-edge choices, but its pendant edge lies on no pentagon and is safe. Restore the minimum-counterexample premise or explicitly exclude both kinds of reductions.
The summary points to the prover-session scratch/REPORT.md rather than the delivered claim/PROOF_REPORT.md. Replace it with the delivered relative link. This does not affect any mathematical claim.
